summary:
**Listing 4.5** compiles the model: `model.compile(optimizer="adam", loss="binary_crossentropy", metrics=["accuracy"])`, exactly the choices justified on p.134.

Section **4.1.4 Validating your approach** starts from a rule learned in chapter 3: a model should never be evaluated on its training data. The standard practice is to hold out a **validation set** to monitor accuracy during training; here, 10,000 samples are set apart from the 25,000 training reviews.

The authors anticipate the question *why not just use the test data?* Because validation results will be used to guide decisions such as model size or number of epochs. Once you do that, the validation score no longer reflects performance on brand-new data: the model has been deliberately modified to do better on it. A set of never-before-seen samples is needed for a final, completely unbiased evaluation, and that is the role of the **test set**. The next chapter develops this further.

**Listing 4.6** performs the split with NumPy slicing: the first 10,000 samples become `x_val`/`y_val`, the remaining 15,000 become `partial_x_train`/`partial_y_train`.

The model is then trained for **20 epochs** (20 passes over all training samples) in **mini-batches of 512**, while loss and accuracy are monitored on the 10,000 held-out samples by passing them as `validation_data` to `model.fit()`. **Listing 4.7** stores the result in `history`, which the next page inspects and plots.

paragraphs.excerpt: As you learned in chapter 3, a deep learning model should never
paragraphs.what_it_says: Never evaluate a model on its training data; use a validation set to monitor accuracy during training. Here 10,000 training samples are set apart for that.
paragraphs.what_it_means: Training accuracy measures memorization as much as learning; only data the model has not trained on tells you how it generalizes.
paragraphs.why_it_matters: Without this, you could not see overfitting, which the next pages reveal in the plots.

terminology.meaning: Held-out data used to monitor and tune the model during development, not for gradient updates.

connections: p.136: The History object records validation metrics per epoch for plotting.

paragraphs.excerpt: You might ask, why not simply use the test data to evaluate
paragraphs.what_it_says: Using the test set for monitoring is tempting but wrong: validation results inform choices like model size and number of epochs, which makes validation scores optimistic. A never-before-seen test set is kept for a final unbiased evaluation; chapter 5 elaborates.
paragraphs.what_it_means: Every decision taken because of a score leaks information from that data into the model. The validation set absorbs that leakage; the test set must stay untouched to remain an honest estimate.
paragraphs.why_it_matters: Information leakage via repeated tuning is one of the most common ways practitioners fool themselves about model quality.
paragraphs.technical_idea: Selecting the best of many configurations on the same data gives an upward-biased estimate of the winner's true performance (selection bias).

terminology.meaning: Data reserved for the single final evaluation.
When evaluation data influences model design, making its scores optimistic (term developed in chapter 5).

connections: p.130: IMDb provides 25,000 training and 25,000 test reviews.

paragraphs.excerpt: You’ll now train the model for 20 epochs (20 iterations over all
paragraphs.what_it_says: Train for 20 epochs (20 iterations over all training samples) in mini-batches of 512, monitoring loss and accuracy on the 10,000 held-out samples via the validation_data argument of model.fit().
paragraphs.what_it_means: Each epoch performs ceil(15000/512) = 30 gradient updates, then evaluates on the validation data, so you get a per-epoch curve of training and validation metrics.
paragraphs.why_it_matters: These per-epoch curves are what reveal when the model starts to overfit.
paragraphs.technical_idea: 20 epochs × 30 steps = 600 updates in total; the last batch per epoch has 15000 − 29·512 = 152 samples.

terminology.meaning: One full pass over the training data.
A subset of samples processed together for one gradient update.
fit() argument: a tuple (x, y) evaluated at the end of every epoch.

concepts.name: Validation set
concepts.definition: Samples held out from training to monitor the model and guide design decisions.
concepts.intuition: Practice exams you take while studying, as opposed to the final exam.
concepts.technical: Here the first 10,000 of 25,000 training samples; evaluated at the end of each epoch.
concepts.significance: Detects overfitting and selects hyperparameters such as epochs.
concepts.misconception: Validation scores are not unbiased once you tune on them.

concepts.name: Test set
concepts.definition: Never-before-seen samples used for the final evaluation round in a completely unbiased way.
concepts.technical: Must not influence any modeling decision.
concepts.significance: The only honest estimate of performance on new data.

concepts.misconception: Checking test accuracy 'just to peek' and then changing the model spoils it.

deeper.title: How tuning on validation data biases it
deeper.body: Beyond the book: suppose you try 50 configurations whose true accuracy is identical, say 88%. Each measured validation score is 88% plus noise. Picking the maximum picks the luckiest noise, so the winner's validation score overstates its real accuracy. The test set, never used in the selection, gives an unbiased estimate of the chosen model.

deeper.title: Practice exams and the final exam
deeper.body: Analogy (not in the book): the training set is the textbook, the validation set is the practice exams you use to decide how to study, and the test set is the final exam. If you studied by memorizing the practice exams, your practice score would mislead you; the final must remain unseen.

takeaways: Listing 4.5: compile with adam, binary_crossentropy and accuracy.
Never evaluate on training data; monitor a validation set.
Do not use the test set to guide choices: tuning on validation data makes it biased, so the test set is kept for a final unbiased evaluation.
